[RDSC.6.8.9] **An omitted pattern binding contributes a placeholder exactly as a
written one does.** Where the author omits a binding ([LGRA.8.1]) the compiler
must interpolate the synthetic name it assigned that pattern, so whether a
binding was written does not affect the template's arity. [RDSC.6.8.5] and
[RDSC.6.8.6] remain the clauses that decide whether a pattern contributes a
placeholder at all.

⚠ **This is the one surface on which a synthetic name reaches an author-facing
display.** [LLEX.10.6.1] gives a synthetic name no surface form, so a reader of a
rendered display name may be shown a `$`-prefixed name they cannot write
themselves. A display name identifies an activation rather than naming it in
source, so the synthetic spelling is admissible there and in no other
author-facing position.
